title: Delinquent day-count 92 from overdue-since 2026-06-01 to business date 2026-09-01 (loan 4)
_note: Parity vector transcribing one non-zero row of the delinquency block read back for SEED-L04 at business date 2026-09-01 under tenant gerege. request.delinquency carries the observed overdue-since civil date 2026-06-01 and the pinned business date 2026-09-01; expect.overdue_days and expect.delinquent_days are TRANSCRIPTIONS of the read-back's delinquent.pastDueDays and delinquent.delinquentDays, both 92. This is the JUNE row: 2026-06-01 -> 2026-09-01 spans June (30) + July (31) + August (31) = 92. It is kept in preference to the other non-zero rows because a 30-day-month approximation (whole months x 30) reads exactly 90 here and disagrees by 2, a port that assumes all three months are 31 reads 93 and disagrees by 1, and a port that stops at the first month boundary reads 30. The 2026-07-01 -> 2026-09-01 = 62 and 2026-08-01 -> 2026-09-01 = 31 rows are separate vectors because each pins a DIFFERENT month-length combination (62 = 31+31, 31 = 31); the duplicate 62 row (loan 5) and the duplicate absent row (loan L06) are NOT cloned. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT GRADE: every observed row has delinquencyPausePeriods empty and delinquentDays == pastDueDays, so paused/grace are both 0 and a port that ignores the subtraction passes; no observed overdue date is after the business date, so the negative clamp in OverdueDays is not exercised either. A capture of a loan with a pause period or a grace setting would be needed. TIME ZONE: the request carries bare calendar dates; loan.OverdueDays resolves them through dateOnly [delinquency.go:96,123], which takes the year/month/day IN THE VALUE'S OWN LOCATION and re-anchors to UTC midnight before subtracting, so no offset is hard-coded. These rows are all midnight-aligned first-of-month civil dates, so they cannot discriminate a UTC-vs-Asia/Ulaanbaatar parse defect; the day difference between two civil dates is zone-independent. Say that rather than claim the zone is covered.

provenance.note: request.delinquency and both expected cells are transcribed from the committed SEED-L04 loan detail read-back loan-4-detail-raw.json. The overdue-since date is the top-level summary.overdueSinceDate array [2026,6,1] -> "2026-06-01"; the expected cells are the delinquent.pastDueDays 92 and delinquent.delinquentDays 92 in the same file (delinquent.delinquentDate is [2026,6,1]). The business date 2026-09-01 is not carried by the detail file; it is the corpus BUSINESS_DATE pinned separately in the seed businessdate capture, cited below. The capture is a single-line JSON document (wc -l = 0), so every observation is at line 1. No value was synthesised: the date and both counts are read directly from the file.

Business date 2026-09-01: .softhouse/capture/seed/out/businessdate-get-raw.json:1 "type":"BUSINESS_DATE","date":[2026,9,1]. Arithmetic: 2026-06-01 -> 2026-09-01 = 30 (June) + 31 (July) + 31 (August) = 92.
